validity.recommendation: keep as operating; no existence/classification/duplicate issue -- see the two spec concerns and one attribution concern below
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independent of GEM/wiki, via FERC's own docket record. FERC Docket No. CP18-332-000 (El Paso Natural Gas Company, L.L.C.) runs through five Federal Register notices I pulled directly from govinfo.gov PDF mirrors (bypassing federalregister.gov's bot-wall): Notice of Intent (2018-06-13, doc 2018-12667), Notice of Application (2018-05-15, doc 2018-10291), Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (2018-08-15, doc 2018-17542), Notice of Availability of the EA (2018-11-20, doc 2018-25285), and a Sunshine Act Meeting Notice (2019-11-19, doc 2019-25127) whose agenda item C-4 lists CP18-332-000/El Paso Natural Gas Company L.L.C. for the Commission's November 21, 2019 open meeting -- independently corroborating the certificate-issuance date KMI's own SEC filings report. Kinder Morgan Inc.'s own SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibits (Q2-2018, Q4-2019, Q2-2020 earnings-release exhibits) track the same project end-to-end: filed April 26, 2018 (~$130M); FERC certificate issued Nov 21, 2019, construction began early December 2019 (~$140M); placed in service July 9, 2020 (~$140M). EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects 1996-2024 sheet, Docket CP18-332) independently matches Length=17mi/Diameter=30in/Capacity=321 MMcf/d exactly. No duplicate found against the 45-row US-gas roster -- P0184 (bare 'El Paso Gas Pipeline', no segment) is the parent/network row, and P2577 (Northern Delaware Basin Expansion) and P3190 (Carlsbad South Project) are other, clearly distinct segment-specific expansions on the same PipelineName; none overlaps this project's docket or facilities. Classification (Gas / transmission / operating) is correct and well-evidenced. Two spec concerns (Capacity's KMI-vs-FERC/EIA figure conflict; SegmentCost's four-way figure conflict) and one attribution/geometry concern (the routes-repo geometry mapped to this PID spans the whole multi-state EPNG South Mainline corridor, not the specific 17-mile Texas-only segment this row's facilities actually describe) are recorded separately below and left for a human decision rather than silently resolved.

contested.Capacity: 321.00 MMcf/d (sheet/FERC/EIA) vs. ~203,000 Dth/d (Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K exhibits, Q2-2018/Q4-2019/Q2-2020, all three repeating the identical figure)

validity.researcher_notes: A genuine, materially large (321 vs 203 MMcf/d-equivalent, ~58% different) capacity conflict exists between two source families for the SAME project. FERC's own Notice of Schedule (Aug 15, 2018): 'would increase the design capacity on El Paso's South Mainline system by 321,000 dekatherms of natural gas per day to Arizona and California delivery points.' EIA's Historical Projects workbook (Docket CP18-332): Additional Capacity = 321 MMcf/d. EIA's own 'Today in Energy' analysis (2020-08, id=44856): 'Providing 0.32 Bcf/d of additional westbound capacity out of the Waha Hub' -- a third, independently-drafted EIA product landing on the same ~320-321 figure. Against this: Kinder Morgan Inc.'s own SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibits for THREE separate quarters (2018-07-18 filing announcement, 2020-01-22 construction-start announcement, 2020-07-22 in-service announcement) all state 'approximately 203,000 Dth/d' verbatim -- internally consistent across 2+ years but a single reporting entity/origin repeated three times, not three independent confirmations. Not overwriting the sheet's recorded 321.00 (it is the better-corroborated figure -- FERC's own regulatory notice plus two independently-produced EIA products, none of which trace to each other or to KMI), but flagging the operator's own repeated, internally-consistent 203,000 Dth/d as a real discrepancy worth a human decision rather than silently discarding it. Possible explanation not confirmed by any source: KMI may be citing INCREMENTAL system throughput net of some offsetting factor, vs. FERC/EIA citing gross authorized design capacity -- but this is speculation, not something any source states.

validity.recommendation: correct SegmentCost from 128,000,000 USD -- no source found matches that figure; propose 140,000,000 USD (KMI's own final/actual-cost figure, stated twice at construction-start and in-service) but flag EIA's conflicting 122,000,000 USD

validity.researcher_notes: Four different cost figures exist across the sources found, and NONE matches the sheet's recorded $128,000,000 exactly. Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K exhibits show the estimate evolving over the project's life: ~$130 million at the April 2018 FERC filing; ~$140 million at both the December 2019 construction start AND the July 2020 in-service announcement (same figure, stated twice, 7 months apart, by the same company -- one origin, not two). Independently, EIA's Historical Projects workbook (compiled from FERC docket filings, last updated 2020-07-06 -- i.e. AFTER the project's completion) records Cost (millions) = 122, a genuinely different, independently-compiled figure that does not trace to KMI's own disclosures. Recommending 140,000,000 USD as the best-supported figure (it is KMI's own actual/near-final cost, reported consistently at two different milestones rather than the earlier ~$130M pre-construction ESTIMATE), but this is a single-origin figure (KMI) and conflicts with EIA's independently-sourced $122M -- neither reaches the 2-independent-agreeing bar, so recording this as a spec CONCERN for human adjudication rather than confidently overwriting the sheet.

validity.recommendation: flag the routes-repo geometry for this PID (aggregate EPNG South Mainline system corridor, TX through southern NM/AZ toward the CA border) as a system-vs-segment mismatch against this row's actual, FERC-described facilities -- no route action taken here (route work is out of scope for this leg; a routes-repo fix needs a separate human-reviewed branch/PR)
validity.researcher_notes: FERC's Notice of Availability of the EA (Nov 20, 2018) itemizes the project's ACTUAL facilities precisely: a new 13,220-hp compressor station in Luna County, New Mexico ('Red Mountain'); a new 13,220-hp compressor station in Cochise County, Arizona ('Dragoon'); and 'approximately 17-miles of 30-inch-outside diameter loop line extension of existing Line 1110 between milepost (MP) 174.5 and MP 191.5 in Hudspeth and El Paso counties, Texas.' So the only LINEAR pipe this project actually built is entirely within Texas -- the NM/AZ facilities are compressor stations only, adding horsepower to the existing mainline without any new pipe mileage there. I inspected data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P2617.geojson in the sibling GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes repo (read-only, per standing rules) and its mapped route spans the ENTIRE EPNG South Mainline corridor (roughly longitude -105.9 to beyond -114.5, i.e. El Paso TX through southern NM/AZ toward the CA border) -- this is the SYSTEM-level route, not this segment's specific facilities, and it is the same corridor P0184 (the bare parent 'El Paso Gas Pipeline' row, no segment) would also plausibly need to represent. This matters directly for the StartState/EndState fill: the batch brief's working assumption that this project's route runs 'Texas -> Arizona' appears to conflate the mapped SYSTEM geometry with the SEGMENT-specific facts -- I filled Location below with Texas/Texas (El Paso and Hudspeth Counties) per the FERC EA's specific facility description, not Texas/Arizona. Not proposing any route-repo edit (route creation/replacement is out of scope for this leg and requires a human-reviewed branch+PR per the routes-repo hard requirement) -- flagging only. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-14: `contested` was keyed 'RouteType/RouteAccuracy (routes repo)', which is not a backend column, so the concern tinted no cell. RouteType is NOT contested: geometry does exist in the routes repo, so 'Mapped route (at any accuracy)' remains correct under the three-way sync rule. The prose that was sitting in the contested value is preserved here: mapped geometry spans the whole multi-state EPNG South Mainline corridor; this project's actual physical facilities are a 17-mile Texas-only loop line plus two out-of-state compressor stations with no linear mileage of their own

fills.researcher_notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to an assumption in the batch guidance: this project's actual physical linear pipe is entirely within TEXAS (Hudspeth and El Paso Counties) -- NOT Texas-to-Arizona. The project's only out-of-Texas facilities (Red Mountain Compressor Station, Luna County NM; Dragoon Compressor Station, Cochise County AZ) are compressor stations, which add horsepower to the existing mainline but contribute no new linear pipe mileage of their own -- so they are not endpoints of THIS row's Length/Diameter-described facility. See the attribution concern in validity[] for the full reasoning (including the mapped routes-repo geometry, which spans the whole multi-state system and should not be read as this segment's specific route). Filling StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea (already 'United States' on the sheet, so those two are unchanged/reconfirmed) plus the previously-blank StartLocation/StartState-Province/EndLocation/EndState-Province. CAVEAT ON ORDERING: FERC's Aug-2018 notice lists the counties as 'El Paso and Hudspeth' while its Nov-2018 EA notice lists them as 'Hudspeth and El Paso' -- the two FERC documents themselves are NOT consistent on order, and neither states a flow direction or which county is the true 'start' vs. 'end.' I am recording El Paso County as Start / Hudspeth County as End for schema completeness, but this ordering is NOT independently confirmed and should not be read as an assertion of physical flow direction. Only one origin (FERC/this docket) names county-level detail at all -- KMI's own disclosures describe the project only at the state level ('Texas, New Mexico and Arizona'), and EIA's workbook Beg_State/End_State (TX/MX) describes the WHOLE multi-facility project's downstream effect (exports reaching Mexico), not this specific segment's physical location -- so that EIA field is deliberately NOT used here (using it would wrongly imply this linear segment reaches Mexico).

summary: P2617 (El Paso Gas Pipeline / South Mainline Expansion Project, FERC Docket CP18-332) is a real, well-documented 2018-2020 EPNG expansion (Kinder Morgan/EPNG) confirmed via 5 Federal Register notices, 3 KMI SEC 8-Ks, and EIA's pipeline-projects workbook + Today-in-Energy article; staged REFS_ADDED on 14 of 15 units (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal=2018-04, Construction=2019-12, Start=2020-07, Capacity=321 MMcf/d, Length=17mi, Diameter=30in, FuelSource=Waha Hub [single-sourced], Location=Texas/Texas [corrects an assumed TX->AZ], SegmentCost corrected 128M->140M, Operator=El Paso Natural Gas Company LLC, Owner=Kinder Morgan 100% confirmed); Pressure is the sole UNRESOLVED unit (no source found). Flagged for human review: (1) a materially large Capacity conflict (FERC/EIA's 321,000 vs. KMI's own repeated 203,000 Dth/d), (2) a 4-way SegmentCost conflict (M sheet / M KMI-estimate / M KMI-actual / M EIA), and (3) a system-vs-segment route-geometry mismatch (P2617's mapped route spans the whole multi-state EPNG corridor while this project's actual linear pipe is a 17-mile Texas-only loop line, with NM/AZ getting compressor stations only) -- cross-referenced to parent row P0184.
